newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet, with light packer bids at $66.00 per cwt passed by owners asking $69.00, feedlot sources said.
Packers were said to be well supplied with live cattle inventory following last week's hefty trade.

Sales were not expected to occur until midweek when packers will be in the market to fill needs for next week, sources said. Fed cattle were seen trading at $68.00 per cwt, possibly higher, amid outlooks for further strength in beef prices, they said. Sales at $68.00 would be $1.00 higher than sales reported Friday, but steady with last week's top.
Beef prices on Friday were quoted up $0.56 to $0.95 per cwt on choice grade supplies and steady to down $0.04 on select, USDA said. There were 227 fabricated beef loads sold.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted up $0.56 at $104.15, which was up $2.22 for the week, USDA statistics showed.
Sales of 227 loads was considered active for a Friday and the fact that the large movement came at higher prices inspired outlooks for firm fed cattle prices this week, several feedlot managers said.
